main_text.p: mò, Rauenæ archiepiscopum secundò, & tertiò (ut sic infano eius amore commodius frueretur) Romanum Papam fecit. Ita erat his diebus, sanctissima mater Ecclesia Romana, meretrici subiecta, ut per illam tota regeretur: sitq; meretrix facta iuxta propheticum scriptum, Apoc.17. Ioannes iste spiritus militares induens, militem potius quàm Episcopum se esse ostendit: ut qui Saracenos, Calabriam, Apuliam, & Italiam deuastantes, sumptis armis, ac multis eorum occisis, his terris expulerit. De cuius fine iterum Liuthprandus, lib.3. cap. 12. sic loquitur: Guido interea, Thusciæ provinciæ Marchio, cum Marozia uxore (prædi-ctæ Theodoræ filia) de Ioannis Papæ deiectione coepit vehementer tractare. Habebat Guido milites multos, Romæ congregatos, qui in Lateranensi palatio anno Domini 928. comprehendentes Papam, custodiæ manciparunt, & cervicale super os eius iniecto, suffocatum illum miserrimè occiderunt. Quo mortuo, prædictum Marozie filium, Ioannem 12. quem ex Sergio Papa meretrix ipsa genuerat, Papam constituerunt. Sic meretricis matris Theodoræ amasium, meretrix Marozia filia, pro filio spurio sublimando, per mariti Guidonis milites peremit. page.notes: The italic setting of the Liutprandus quotation (from "Guido interea" to "occiderunt.") is my reading of the scan and is uncertain; the rest of the page looks roman. "prædi-ctæ" at the line end is partly doubtful: the ligature "ct" was hard to read, but the hyphenation looks right. "Marozie" is copied as printed. The last word, "consenferant", is split across the page: "consenfe-" is on the page, and "rant," is the catchword at the foot. The "Ioannem 12." reference and "lib.3. cap. 12." are inline in the text, not marginal notes.
